questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The principal as well as the teachers / were present / at the annual day function / in the school auditorium.
options: The principal as well as the teachers
questions.explanation: With 'as well as', 'along with', 'together with', the verb agrees with the FIRST subject (the principal, singular). So 'was present' is correct.
questions.shortcut: as well as / along with: verb follows the first subject.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Each of the students / have submitted / the project report / before the deadline.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb, so 'has submitted' is correct.
questions.shortcut: Each / every / either / neither + singular verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Neither Ravi nor his brothers / is willing / to join / the cricket team.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Brothers' is plural, so 'are willing' is required.
questions.shortcut: Neither-nor: verb agrees with the noun right next to it.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The news about the floods / were / very disturbing / to everyone.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb, so 'was' is correct.
questions.shortcut: news, mathematics, physics, gallows = singular.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Mathematics / are / my favourite subject / in school.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects such as mathematics, physics and economics are singular, so the verb must be 'is'.
questions.shortcut: Subject names ending in -s still take 'is'.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She prefers tea / than coffee / in the morning / before going to work.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than': prefer X to Y. The correct phrase is 'to coffee'.
questions.shortcut: prefer X TO Y (never than).

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: I have been living / in Coimbatore / since five years / and I like it.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point of time (since 2015); 'for' is used with a period (for five years).
questions.shortcut: since = point in time, for = duration.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He is senior / than me / by two years / in the company.
questions.explanation: 'Senior', 'junior', 'superior', 'inferior' are followed by 'to', not 'than': 'senior to me'.
questions.shortcut: senior / junior / superior / inferior + TO.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The furniture in the hall / were / recently / polished.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'was recently polished'.
questions.shortcut: furniture, luggage, scenery, information: uncountable, singular.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Hardly had he reached the station / than the train / started moving / slowly.
options: Hardly had he reached the station
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' and 'scarcely' are followed by 'when'; 'no sooner' is followed by 'than'. So 'when the train' is correct.
questions.shortcut: Hardly / scarcely ... WHEN; no sooner ... THAN.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: One of the best players / of our team / have / been selected for the state squad.
options: been selected for the state squad.
questions.explanation: 'One of the + plural noun' takes a singular verb: the subject is 'one'. Correct: 'has been selected'.
questions.shortcut: One of + plural noun -> singular verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The number of applicants / for the clerical posts / are / increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular, so the verb is 'is'. ('A number of' would be plural.)
questions.shortcut: The number of = singular; A number of = plural.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: A number of students / was / absent / due to the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb: 'were absent'.
questions.shortcut: A number of = plural; The number of = singular.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The teacher along with her students / are going / on a field trip / to Mysuru.
options: The teacher along with her students
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'the teacher'. Correct: 'is going'.
questions.shortcut: along with / together with: ignore the added noun.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Many a student / have / failed / in the first attempt.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: 'Many a student has failed'.
questions.shortcut: Many a + singular noun + singular verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Fifty rupees / are / too much / for this notebook.
questions.explanation: A sum of money, distance or time treated as one amount takes a singular verb: 'Fifty rupees is too much'.
questions.shortcut: Sum / distance / time as one unit -> singular.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Two-thirds of the land / in this village / are / under cultivation.
questions.explanation: With fractions, the verb agrees with the noun after 'of'. 'Land' is uncountable (singular), so 'is under cultivation' is correct.
questions.shortcut: Fraction + of + noun: verb matches the noun.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Why did he / not told / me about / the change in schedule?
questions.explanation: After 'did' the main verb takes its base form: 'did not tell'.
questions.shortcut: did / does / do + base verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The police / has / arrested / the suspect.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is always plural, so the verb must be 'have arrested'.
questions.shortcut: police, cattle, people = plural.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He asked me / that where / I was going / at that hour.
questions.explanation: In reported questions the question word itself introduces the clause; 'that' must not be added: 'He asked me where I was going'.
questions.shortcut: Reported question: no 'that' with wh-words.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The cost of living / in metropolitan cities / are rising / faster than in towns.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the cost' (singular); 'of living' and 'in cities' are modifiers. Correct: 'is rising'.
questions.shortcut: Find the head noun; ignore the phrase after it.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: I would have gone / to the match / if he would have / invited me.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'if + past perfect, would have + past participle'. Correct: 'if he had invited me'.
questions.shortcut: if-clause never takes 'would'.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: If I was / you, I would / apologise to / the manager immediately.
questions.explanation: An imaginary (unreal) condition uses the subjunctive 'were' for all persons: 'If I were you'.
questions.shortcut: Unreal if-clause: If I WERE.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She is looking forward / to meet / her cousin / next month.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and must be followed by a gerund: 'to meeting'.
questions.shortcut: look forward TO + -ing.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The manager suggested / me to take / a few days off / after the audit.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' cannot take 'object + to-infinitive'. Correct: 'suggested that I take' or 'suggested my taking'.
questions.shortcut: suggest never takes 'me to ...'.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He is one of those players / who has / never missed / a practice session.
options: He is one of those players
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'players' (plural), not 'one'. Correct: 'who have never missed'.
questions.shortcut: one of those + plural noun + who + PLURAL verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Neither of the two candidates / were / suitable for / the post.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' with a plural noun takes a singular verb in standard usage: 'Neither of the two candidates was suitable'.
questions.shortcut: Neither of / either of -> singular verb.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Between you and I / the plan / is not / practical at all.
questions.explanation: A preposition takes the object form of the pronoun: 'between you and me'.
questions.shortcut: Preposition + me / him / her / us / them.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She is more intelligent / than any / other girls / in her class.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' must be followed by a singular noun in this comparison: 'any other girl'.
questions.shortcut: Comparative + any other + SINGULAR noun.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: This is the most unique / painting that / I have ever seen / in a gallery.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' means one of a kind, so it cannot be graded with 'most' or 'more'. Correct: 'This is a unique painting'.
questions.shortcut: unique, perfect, complete: no 'most / very'.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The old man / was so weak / that he cannot / walk without support.
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the past ('was'), so the result clause must also be in the past: 'could not'.
questions.shortcut: Past main clause -> past in the subordinate clause.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Had I known / about the delay, I / will have / started earlier.
questions.explanation: In 'Had I known ...' (third conditional inverted) the result is 'would have + past participle'. 'Will have' is wrong.
questions.shortcut: Had + subject + pp -> would have + pp.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The reason for his failure / is because / he did not / prepare properly.
questions.explanation: 'The reason ... is that' is the correct pattern; 'because' repeats the idea of reason.
questions.shortcut: reason ... is THAT, never because.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Not only the students / but also the teacher / were / disappointed with the result.
questions.explanation: With 'not only ... but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the teacher' (singular): 'was disappointed'.
questions.shortcut: Not only-but also: nearer subject decides.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The sceneries / of Kerala / are / breathtaking.
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form. Correct: 'The scenery of Kerala is breathtaking'.
questions.shortcut: scenery, furniture, luggage, advice: no plural -s.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He gave me / many informations / about the / admission process.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: 'a lot of information' / 'much information'.
questions.shortcut: information, advice, knowledge: no -s.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: All the luggages / were loaded / onto the / waiting truck.
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable and cannot take -s. Correct: 'All the luggage was loaded'.
questions.shortcut: luggage / baggage: never plural.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She did not know / whether he / will come / or not.
questions.explanation: The main verb is in the past ('did not know'), so the noun clause needs 'would come' (sequence of tenses).
questions.shortcut: Past + reporting -> will becomes would.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: I congratulate you / for your / success in / the examination.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' takes 'on' for the occasion: 'congratulate you on your success'.
questions.shortcut: congratulate ON.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She was accused / for theft / by the shop owner / last week.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse' is followed by 'of': 'accused of theft'.
questions.shortcut: accuse OF; charge WITH.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He is very much / fond for / cricket and / plays daily.
questions.explanation: 'Fond' is followed by 'of': 'fond of cricket'.
questions.shortcut: fond OF; good AT; afraid OF.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The sun rises / in the east and / sets in the west. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: Universal truths take the simple present, and all agreements are correct, so the sentence has no error.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Each of the boys / has completed / his assignment. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb ('has') and the singular pronoun 'his'; the sentence is correct.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Neither the captain / nor the players / were told the schedule. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'players' (plural), so 'were' is correct.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The number of vacancies / has increased / this year. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, so 'has increased' is correct.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Had she known the truth, / she would have / acted differently. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'Had + subject + past participle, would have + past participle'. The sentence is correct.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: I prefer walking / to driving / in this heavy traffic. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: 'Prefer X to Y' with two gerunds is correct, so there is no error.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Hardly had we reached / the hall when / the lights went out. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' is the correct pair and the inversion is correct.

questions.questionText: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She has been working / here / since January. (If the sentence is correct, choose No error.)
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous with 'since' plus a point in time is correct.
